business_problem: Broughton Partners needed to move mass-tort claimant cases through its intake and confirmation work quickly while maintaining high case quality. Its audit work required distinguishing checks suited to predictable deterministic logic from those where AI reasoning could help, without surrendering human judgment on discrepancies.
solution_summary: Broughton Partners connects mass-tort law firms with qualified claimants through lead generation, intake qualification, and claim confirmation, with quality and compliance at the center of the service. It needed to move cases out quickly without lowering the quality its clients expect. The Salesforce deployment uses 18 Agentforce agents to increase daily audit capacity and improve case quality. The team assigns checks according to whether they require deterministic logic or AI reasoning, their operating cost, and tolerance for error; AI is used for interpretation while clear-cut decisions remain predictable. Agents surface discrepancies with their reasoning, but Broughton staff make the final decision, keeping human review in the workflow and focusing staff on cases needing intervention. Salesforce lists Mulesoft and Apex, but the story gives no deployment roles for them and describes no ingestion, storage, model configuration, or external integrations.

evidence_quotes: We had to figure out a way to get these cases out the door as quickly as possible while maintaining the high quality of cases that we are known for.
2 x daily audit capacity while improving quality with 18 Agentforce Agents

A critical part of building confidence was knowing the agents would not make the final call on a discrepancy. They surfaced it for review, showed the reasoning, and Elizabeth’s team made the decision.
We looked at each check through three lenses: whether it needed deterministic logic or AI reasoning, the cost of running it, and how much room there was for error.
